To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the proposed n-gram language model based session identification approach significantly outperforms the traditional ad hoc fixed timeout approach for association rule mining in the Livelink logs.

1) the n-gram language model is a useful tool in the context of session detection; 2) the use of the language model for this purpose leads to significant improvements over traditional session detection methods; 3) the language model can be applied in an online fashion, which is a significant advantage over the traditional timeout method; 4) the language model provides a dynamic approach to session detection; and 5) the language model is a robust technique for session detection.
we have developed a novel method for session boundary detection that significantly improves the results obtained from association rule learning on a large collection of web log data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of identifying session boundaries in a collection of log data.
the problem of session identification for association rule learning in large collections of web log data.
developing a statistical model to detect session boundaries in a log file and using these session boundaries in association rule learning.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our approach is able to identify more relevant sessions, and that the identified sessions are of higher quality.
our method is a statistically sound and effective method for identifying sessions in a large collection log files.
the proposed session detection technique is a significant improvement on the standard timeout method.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the n-gram based session identification method is a promising technique for association rule learning on Livelink logs.

we have developed a method for session identification in a log file that is based on the information theoretic approach of n-gram language modeling and that this method can be used in association rule learning.
the n-gram language model is a promising approach for session boundary detection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have demonstrated the utility of using a dynamic session identification method in the context of association rule learning.
the n-gram approach can be used as a general method for identifying session boundaries in log data for any application that uses association rule learning.

we can use n-gram language modelling to identify sessions in large collections of web log data, and that the sessions identified by this approach are more effective for association rule learning than those identified by the traditional timeout approach.
